tei:titleStmt.tei:title: Prayer of the Guest Chaplain of the U.S. Senate: Rabbi Dr. Joshua Loth Liebman on 19 May 1948

tei:div.tei:head: Prayer of the Guest Chaplain of the U.S. Senate: Rabbi Dr. Joshua Loth Liebman on 19 May 1948

tei:lg.tei:l: O God, Father of all men,
for this great Senate of democracy
that men shall live by them
to make America an ever more beautiful gem of earth
where cooperation shall be the dream
and equal justice the dynamic goal—
America thus the example to all the world.
from the oldest unto the newest, Israel,
dwell today on the same street of atomic destiny,
and therefore we must live and work together
shall have a planet to inherit.
to build the wider mansion of human welfare—
where all Thy children shall live together

tei:note.tei:p: The Israeli Declaration of Independence was announced only five days prior, on 14 May 1948.

A quotable phrase from an address offered before Hadassah on 25 October 1947 by Rabbi Abba Hillel Silver (head of the American section of the Jewish Agency for Palestine and chairman of the American Zionist Emergency Council). “A positive decision at the United Nations will be a victory for the United States and for the Soviet Union... These two great powers have been brought together on the Palestine issue while they fail to see eye to eye on almost every other issue. For the Jewish people, an affirmative decision will mean the beginning of a new epoch in history. The manner in which the Arab peoples react to the decision of the United Nations will also have great consequences for them. It may mean prolonged and costly conflict which will benefit no one, or it may mean cooperating for the regeneration of the entire Near East for the blessing of all and the hurt of none.”
